why: Validates the TYPE instead of the domain, the plausible way to write this guard (issue #1058; modelled on settings-accepts-an-unknown-quality-preset). Any string is then stored, persisted and published, and the next match indexes `OWNER_PALETTES` with it, handing every ring, chip and vignette reader `undefined`. It also breaks the refusal contract the store rests on: a refused value publishes nothing, which is what keeps a control showing what was actually accepted.
killedBy: createPlayerSettingsStore: validation refuses an off-domain SETTER argument and keeps the accepted value
createPlayerSettingsStore: defaults and persistence does NOT publish a refused value
